stat: Reduction in the number of integrations to build when a UK enterprise connects AI tools to its core systems via MCP instead of point-to-point APIs
unit: percent fewer integrations (15 vs 105, for a 15-system enterprise stack)
method: Recipe A (adapted) — mathematical derivation applying the standard M x N vs M + N integration-complexity formula (as described in MCP's own architecture rationale) to a concrete worked example
workings: For N systems needing full pairwise connectivity, point-to-point integration requires N(N-1)/2 unique connections. For N=15: 15 x 14 / 2 = 105 connections. Under MCP, each of the 15 systems exposes one MCP server, so the AI side needs only N=15 connections regardless of how many AI tools are added later. Reduction: (105-15)/105 = 90/105 = 0.857, rounded to 86%. This is an illustrative worked example using a stated assumption of 15 core systems, not a claimed average across UK enterprises; the underlying formula and its direction (M x N collapsing to M + N) is standard integration-architecture reasoning that MCP's own documentation uses to explain the protocol's purpose.
